newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by an expected increase in marketings, livestock dealers said.

Weakness also was expected amid ideas that packer demand would be light following gains in cash hog prices late this week and sluggish pork demand, which pushed packer operating margins into the red, market sources said.
Pork processing plants would operate at about break-even levels at hog prices of about $51.50, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds on Friday.
Hogs sold in Iowa on Friday at a top of $55.00 per cwt.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices at plants could range from $54.50 to $55.00. Illinois plant prices were seen ranging from $53.50 to $54.00, dealers said.
Marketings in most of Illinois Friday were limited by slick roads which could result in greater numbers of hogs moved Monday once transportion difficulties ease, they said.
However, possible price declines from the large movement could be offset by demand from packing plants which had trouble gathering hog inventories on Friday, the dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices at plants Monday could range from $52.00 to $52.50, depending on hog movement, buyers said.
